name: diesel_engine_excess_air_exhaust_analysis
title: Diesel engine: excess air and useful power from exhaust-gas analysis
summary: Combustion of diesel fuel (CH_n, n fitted from C/H mass fractions) with excess air; the excess air follows from the fuel-air ratio and the useful power from the five-box energy balance of the course, with the products brought to the exhaust temperature of 432 °C.

authors: TBD (ULiège, MECA0002 Thermodynamique appliquée, course of S. Quoilin)

verification.reference: EES stored solution of the source file (58 variables, --ees-units) and the Python/CoolProp solution of the same exercise in the collection (2018-2019 repetition folder); the comparison concerns the runnable variant diesel_engine_excess_air_exhaust_analysis_coolsolve.eescode, the native file being blocked
verification.notes: Native file: 'Unknown fluid: CarbonMonoxide' (CS-GAP-FLUIDS-ALIAS), square system otherwise (58/58). Variant vs EES: 9 of 58 variables differ above rtol=0.001: absolute enthalpies on different reference states (EES real-fluid anchors vs CoolProp; real-fluid CarbonMonoxide vs ideal-gas CO; air_ha vs Air) and q_O2 at 1.78e-03 (real-fluid O2, within the 0.5 % EES-vs-CoolProp tolerance). All differences and derived results agree: e, lambda, far, Q_dot_utile within 5e-06 to 8e-05. Python/CoolProp prints e = 89.4 %, lambda = 189.4 %, Q_dot_utile = -106.9 kW, as the variant.

history.action: correction (orchestrator review): CarbonMonoxide (EES real fluid) restored in the native file, status blocked by CS-GAP-FLUIDS-ALIAS; the CO version shipped as the runnable _coolsolve variant
